correctness.rationale: Read the complete source RESULT.md and verify_cone_endpoint.py. Every diametral pair consists of vertices and a chord approaching D localizes at finitely many diameter lines. At each endpoint, any nonzero tangent vector v has a strictly positive axial inner product with the diameter direction; compactness on the polyhedral cone gives a uniform lower bound, so endpoint displacement is O(eps). Crossing-plane coordinates y_a,y_b in e-perp give the invariant line Jacobian D^(-q)(1+||y_b-y_a||²/D²)^(-(d+1)/2). The local axial gauge gives limiting deficit g_Qa(y_a)+g_Qb(y_b) and the beta integral has volume (q!)²/(2q)! times vol Qa vol Qb. Cauchy normalization yields exactly 2(q!)²/[ (2q)! kappa_q S(K) D^q ] times the diameter-pair sum. Independently verified the regular-simplex Gram determinant det(2I_q+J_q)=2^(q-1)(q+2) and the closed coefficients for d=4,5,6 (d4=0.2250790790392766). Unlike finite sampling, these analytical geometry and dominated-convergence steps support the universal quantifiers. The sampling model is explicitly invariant random lines, not uniform endpoints.

value.rationale: A genuinely universal high-dimensional endpoint law for a natural Crofton chord distribution: the exponent is polytope-universal but the positive coefficient decomposes into local tangent-cone sections at diameter pairs. The formula cleanly generalizes previously computed orthotope subclasses and supplies a sharp simplex benchmark; it is not an arbitrary dimension or numerical instance.

scientific_limitations: A general older high-dimensional Crofton endpoint asymptotic may be less searchable than special-polytope cases.
The law applies only to Euclidean-motion invariant lines and polytopes; smooth bodies and endpoint-sampling conventions may have different exponents.
